deck_context.source_summary: Week 03 teaches students to read a two-loop Kirchhoff matrix as a compact representation of physical equations before solving in MATLAB.
deck_context.core_claim: A coefficient is trustworthy only when its value, sign, matrix position, and physical origin agree.

slides.title: Audit the matrix before asking MATLAB to solve
slides.intent: Make the matrix-entry-to-audit-row mapping unambiguous with four independent non-crossing arrows.
key_points: Every arrow must terminate at the centre of the matching Entry row, not at the Value or Physical origin columns.

required_images.role: approved revised Week 03 sample slide style reference
required_images.fidelity: match style only; do not copy exact layout or content
preserve the title, matrix entries, table content, values, signs, units, physical-origin text, and lower takeaway; correct the connector geometry and origin anchors
preserve A11=3 Ω, A12=−1 Ω, A21=−1 Ω, A22=4 Ω and every physical-origin statement exactly

slides.layout: retain the matrix on the left and the strict audit table on the right, but create a clear connector gutter with four independent mapping arrows
slides.visual_elements: four separate coloured arrows map A11→row 1, A12→row 2, A21→row 3, and A22→row 4; each arrow has its own source dot and arrowhead
slides.source_image_rules: Use the current Slide 06 as the edit base. Use the audit table as a strict source. The arrows are semantic mapping arrows, not circuit-current arrows.
constraints: A11→row 1, A12→row 2, A21→row 3, and A22→row 4; every arrowhead points to the centre of the matching Entry cell.
Use separate source dots on the correct coefficient cells. A21 must begin on A21, never on A22; A22 must remain visually independent.
No shared segments, shared junctions, crossings, or arrow paths that touch another coefficient cell.

Follow the specialist geometry: A11 rises to its row centreline then travels right; A12 is a straight horizontal arrow; A21 rises from its top edge, travels above A22 to the gutter, drops to row 3, then turns right; A22 drops below the matrix then travels right along row 4.
Keep the semantic colour map: blue for A11/A22, ochre for A12, sage for A21. Matching cell, coefficient number, connector, and row tint must use the same colour.
Do not point to the Value or Physical origin columns, and do not make the arrows look like a physical circuit path.
No slide number, outer frame, watermark, unrelated logo, or altered numerical content.
